text: Andar Beech was the High Artificer of Gond in Baldur's Gate during the late 15 century DR. He led over one hundred Gondar priests and acolytes within the grand High House of Wonders in the city's Temples District. High Artificer Beech took over the post after the former head priest, Torlin Silvershield, was revealed to be an abomination of the returned deity Bhaal.
Khedive Aman al-Qasi abu Nari was the ruler of Kadarasto in 1367 DR.
Amaril Sweetwater was a half-elf and former adventurer whose travels eventually led her to Elventree. She liked the sylvan community so much that she decided to stay.
Andalias was a man who ran a currency-conversion business in Zhentil Keep around 1369 DR.
Amethyst Trueblood was a gnome priestess active in the 14 century DR.
Amgrel Vlorund was a priest of Auril in the late 15 century DR who hailed from the city of Fireshear.

Amstor the Grim was a halfling cleric of Arvoreen that worked as a priest and administrator at Holyhands House in the North Ward of Waterdeep in the . He and his two brothers were known as the Defenders Three.
Ameralis Zauviir was a drow cleric who had a connection with the Watcher's Keep in the mid–14 century DR.

Angrath Dree was the owner and operator of Old Angrath's Smokehouse in Red Larch, northwest Faerûn, circa the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR. She was also skilled in alchemy and sold potions and ointments that she made herself.
Ander was a clerk who worked at Barthen's Provisions in the late 15 century DR.
Andilal Tharimpar, also called the Stout, was the Nessarch of Yhaunn in Sembia in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Andorn was a looter that worked for the gnome Gimblebock in the late 15 century DR.
Anwat al-Makkar was a skilled sa'luk and sheikh of the House of Dhi'b tribe in the High Desert of west Zakhara around 1367 DR.

Araunglauth was a massive beholder and a member of the Zhentarim in the 13 and 14 centuries DR. Araunglauth lived by the river Tesh in the valley of Arntethyl in Desertsmouth Mountains in the Dalelands from around 1288 DR. An ally of Manshoon by 1358 DR, it aided Ruatheene's rule.
Queen Arhymeria Ithal was the wife of King Nishan Ithal II of Tethyr.
Arktash was an orc chieftain of the Il-Khan tribe that made its home in the Spine of the World, around the 14th century DR.
Arash bint Sanjar was a Grand Caliph of Zakhara, ruling from the Enlightened Throne in the mid–7th century DR. He was the daughter of Sanjar.
Aravilar Moondown was a moon elf Knight of the Weave who served with the order during the 14 century DR. He was extremely dedicated to the Weave and magic throughout his years of service.

Argrum Blackspear was a bandit leader in Tethyr in 1358 DR who preyed upon the Trade Way. He once clashed with the Company of Eight. He tried to gather all bandit leaders of the area to form an alliance, hoping to also attract the Company of Eight so that he could eliminate them. He had a knack for organization, which made him a good leader.
Ardanthe was one of the Nimbral Lords. She was a motherly figure and one of the leading Elders.
Ardethra Murmarand was a cleric of Chauntea with the rank of Watchful that resided in the Bounty of the Goddess temple in Voonlar.
Arauntan of Selgaunt (the Wandering Wizard) was a wizard from Selgaunt. He is notable because in 1351 DR, he recalled that three brothers in Harrowdale had dramatically changed their appearance.
Arizza was the bookkeeper of the Xanathar Thieves' Guild in Skullport in 1479 DR.
Arbenita Darkwind, mostly known as Benita, was an evil cleric of Malar in Undermountain in 1375 DR.
Argens Bruil was the heir of House Bruil in Melvaunt in 1374 DR.
Aravae Irithyl was the lost heiress of the coronal Eltargrim Irithyl and the first sign of the Fall of Myth Drannor.
Ardsem Skalarn was a member of the Zhentarim in Mulmaster in 1373 DR.
Argast was a promising young malaugrym in the mid–14 century DR.
Arender was a legendary gnome architect and builder who lived in Tarmalune, one of the Windrise Ports of Laerakond.
Arkhan the Cruel () was a dragonborn oathbreaker paladin of Tiamat who lived in the late 15 century DR.
Asharak was a tiefling of Elturel that was forced from his home city along with others of his kind in the late 15 century DR.
Artoth Frayhammer was the dwarven architect who built the Great Hall of Myth Drannor long before the advent of the Weeping War.
Arnuth was a Ffolk stablemaster inhabiting the town of Aithelar in Callidyrr on the Moonshae Isles in .
Aruugan was chieftain of the hobgoblin Black Wolf clan of the Giantspire Mountains as of the .
Artiuk was a loyal half-orc bodyguard to the tiefling merchant Vadin'ya of Samargol circa 1374 DR.
Arn Rockfist Akannathi was the chieftain of the Akannathi goliaths of Skytower Shelter during the late 15 century DR.
Goodwife Aruna was a cleric of Chauntea who settled in the hamlet of West Harbor in the Mere of Dead Men circa 1374 DR.
Arlathna was one of the elven mages who fell at the hands of Horaundoon the Eater-of-Mantles of the Zhentarim in 1348 DR.
Arn Widdens was an owner of the Cart and Coin caravan outfitter in Triboar in the Dessarin Valley in the late 15 century DR.
Artagalor Goldbeard was an dwarf jeweler and shopkeeper inhabiting the city of Zhentil Keep during the late–14 century DR.
Ascot Stumblefoot was a halfling shopkeeper inhabiting the city of Zhentil Keep during the late 14 century DR.
Arundoom was a mage who inhabited the city of Waterdeep at an undertermined time.
Armult Tesper was a noble and patriach of the Waterdhavian noble house Tesper during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Asavir was an infamous legendary pirate from the Nelanther Isles and the namesake of Asavir's Channel, active in the early 11 century DR.
Arlburt Nammond was a cobbler from Hultail in Cormyr, active in the late 15 century DR.

Arrant Quill was a renowned bard and member of the Harpers. He was famously imprisoned within a demiplane that resembled his home village, in order prevent him and those he cared about, from succumbing to the effects of an ancient cursed artifact.
Arpeggi Trill (not his real name) was a Sembite half-elf adventurer and bard who was part of the Ruby Blades adventuring company in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Asheera was an elf paladin from the world of Azallah who went on a quest to find and stop Morag of the Old Ones. After entering the Source Stone, in the demiplane there, she met the Hero of Neverwinter, who was on the same mission, in the .
Arlho was a brewer and merchant inhabiting the town of Ashabenford in Mistledale during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Armond Arhesian was a reporter who wrote for the Ravens Bluff Trumpeter broadsheet in Ravens Bluff in the late 14 century DR.
Arroc was a mage member of the Wizards Guild of Ravens Bluff, active in the late 14 century DR.
Artimezt was a drow mercenary who accompanied Dhourn Ba'Tol during his search for the legendary Adamantine Forge.
Arlen Bormul was a member of the Bormul family in the late 13 and early 14 century DR who contributed to the collapse of the kingdom of Amn and directly caused the extinction of the Parhek dynasty.
Arthur Billfold was an art connoisseur who once lived in the city of Baldur's Gate, sometime in the late 15 century DR.
Art Cullagh was a member of the Flaming Fist who served Grand Duke Eltan in the late 14 century DR.
Arrias was a Netherese arcanist who was the Dean of Teachers at the Variator's Intelligentsia in Eileanar in Netheril before its destruction in .
Arls Beatorh was a vintner merchant from the city of Athkatla in Amn who lived some years before the 15 century DR.

Ashen Rock was a male tabaxi scout who resided in the Malar's Throat slums of Port Nyanzaru, Chult, during the late 15 century DR. He was a member of Port Nyanzaru's Citizens' Brigade and worked to defend the residents of Malar's Throat from the dangers of the jungle.
Ashtha Gheldieg was a member of the Amnian House Gheldieg from the city of Eshpurta in the late 15 century DR.
Arlond Stormserpent was a nobleman of House Stormserpent sometime prior to the late 15 century DR.

Artemis () was a multispheric interloper deity of hunting, young women, childbirth, wild beasts, and all manner of wild things. Some also associated her with the moon, but it only rarely counted among her portfolio. There was no evidence that this deity was directly worshiped in the Realms.
Arvas or Avras was a warrior in the Frostfire Banner adventuring party during the mid–8 century DR.
Arman Argentine was a dwarven member of the Tethyamar expedition during the 1480s DR.
Arne Jacobson was a commoner from the Rivington district of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Aryvindaire was a trader and a leader of a wood elven band that resided within the Neverwinter Wood in the late 14 century DR.
Aryn Vasar was a hunter operating out of Port Nyanzaru in Chult during the late 15 century DR.
Arnthiir Windrivv was an adventuring human bard of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, and a member of the Nine.
Arves Silvermount was a client of the Sharran House of Grief and an inhabitant of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Artemus Dimartius was a human swashbuckler living in Waterdeep in the mid 14 century DR.
Arthius was a male half-sun elf musician who resided in Silverymoon during the late 15 century DR.
Asglyn was an adventurer and cleric of Tempus during the early-to-mid–3 century DR. He was a member of the Brave Blades.
Ashanda was an evening-lass at The Kissing Wench in Athalantar in the Western Heartlands during the early-to-mid–3 century DR.
Arthlach was an Axelord of Westdelve in the early 3 century DR.
Arlon was a mage of the Cult of the Dragon during the late 14 century DR.
Asglarek was the ruler of the goblin kingdom of Chalarstaukh in the Rauvin Mountains in the late 14 century DR.
Armando was a famed adventuring duelist, owner of enchanted Armando's dueling boots, who made a name for himself in or before the 14 century DR.
Arno and Julian were the two heads of a single being, the origin of the ettin race.

Arumn Gardpeck was the owner of the tavern called The Cutlass in Luskan. He took in the famed barbarian Wulfgar when he was battling with his personal demons after being imprisoned by the balor Errtu.

Arphoind Bleth was the leader of the Bleth family around the time of Azoun IV's death. He was the second known Arphoind of the Bleth family, likely named after Arphoind Bleth I from the earliest days of Cormyr.
Avan Vatsisen was a Thayan wizard active in the early 1370s DR.
Auppenser was a stoic god, and the precepts of his worship included moderation, inner balance, self-reflection, and reason.
Aunadar Bleth was a human noble of the Bleth family of Cormyr.
Asper was an inhabitant of Waterdeep and the wife of Mirt around 1373 DR.

Atreus Eleint was a wealthy human noble and the descendant of an unknown noble family living in Erlkazar. A spell used on him in his youth had distorted his growth and caused him to become severely deformed, not detracting much from his physical abilities but ruining his appearance. This virtual handicap prevented him from living a normal life and caused him to become obsessed with trying to become handsome. Eventually, he joined the church of Sune, asking for a miracle, and was sent on an impossible quest to the Utter East to find the valley of Langdarma.
Prior Athosar was a human cleric and morninglord of Lathander at the Spires of the Morning temple in Waterdeep in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Athrogate was a dwarf warrior of some reputation in the Bloodstone Lands and later in the North. He later became a companion of Jarlaxle and an agent of Bregan D'aerthe.

Ava Moonflower was a moon elf of House Moonflower long before the Crown Wars of the ancient realm Aryvandaar. She was also a mighty High Mage and served as a center for the high magic rituals. She was married to the sun elf Rolim Durothil shortly before both traveled the ocean with many elves to the island of Evermeet. Their marriage was arranged, because her husband had little magical aptitude to pass it down to his children and his father wanted his new wife to bring that into his family. At the beginning of the voyage both had their problems with that arrangement but during the travel they learned to respect and love each other. Four hundred years later, after the death of the High Counci

Atherton Cooper, better known as Sneakabout, was a halfling thief of the village of Black Oaks in Cormyr in the mid–14 century DR. Playing a part in the Time of Troubles, he wielded the magic sword Godsbane before it was stolen from him by the mortal Cyric.
Auro'pol Dyrr was the matron mother of House Agrach Dyrr of Menzoberranzan in the mid–14 century DR.
Autton Shadowshroud was a male elven assassin and a member of the Shadowkind assassin guild based in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the 1360s DR.

Aubrin Crownsilver, who usually went by his nickname "Brin", was a young acolyte of Torm and a scion of the Crownsilver noble family of Cormyr in the late 15 century DR. Due to his grandmother's dalliance with a prince of Cormyr, his father was a bastard Obarskyr, which, under Cormyrean law and rules of succession, placed the acolyte fourth in the line for the throne as of 1479 DR.
Athorton was a sage from Nleeth on Vilhon Reach, living in the 13th century DR.

Asuras were good messenger spirits in service to deities, and as such were the main competitors to the devas. They were a symbol of goodness and light, kindness and tenderness, and often appeared on the Material Plane helping mystics and faithful.

At'ar the Merciless, also known as the Yellow Goddess, was a Bedine deity. She was the sun goddess of the Bedine. She was depicted as an old, spiteful woman. The Bedine believed she was married to Kozah (Talos), but she was having an affair with N'asr, the Lord of the Dead. Whenever night falls, according to the Bedine, it was At'ar forsaking her lawful husband to sleep in the tent of the Lord of the Dead. In retribution, Kozah sent storms that represented the god's fury at his wife's faithless nature. In the Age of Netheril, she was known as Amaunator, a male sun god. As At'ar, she tended to ignore her worshipers among the Bedine.
Aubaudameira Dree, usually known as Alais, was a female elf who was the herald of the Coronal Eltargrim of Cormanthyr in the 3 century DR.
Asraf yn Malik el Kahaman yi Manshaka was one of the most prominent members of the Moonstars in the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR.
Aunrae Dhuurniv was the eldest of the Matron Sisters of House Dhuurniv involved in the Zhent invasion of Shadowdale in the Year of Risen Elfkin, 1375 DR.

Aunrae Nasadra was the matron mother of House Nasadra and the uncrowned queen of Ched Nasad until its fall in the year 1372 DR. According to the House's tradition many of the direct line were named 'Aunrae'.

Atatlab Xorlarrin was a warrior of House Xorlarrin of Menzoberranzan in 1372 DR. Atatlab was one of the sentries patrolling the house compound during the Silence of Lolth. Matron Mother Zeerith Q'Xorlarrin knew him by name.
Atabeg al-Mazdaghani was a noble marid who lived under the waters of the island of Al-Zira in the Djinni's Claws in 1367 DR.
Ataman al-Hajar was a noble dao who lived deep within an intricate cave system on the island of Al-Zira in the Djinni's Claws in 1367 DR.

Aumon Baenre was the elder boy of matron mother Quenthel Baenre circa 1484 DR. He was in his first year at Tier Breche. He was secretly approached by the Jaezred Chaulssin, who coerced him into eventually revolting against his mother.
Ausitil was a Queen of Dambrath during the mid–13 century DR.
Athalee was an elf living in Kryptgarden Forest in past ages.
Astrid Saj () was a wealthy merchant in Mulmaster in 1491 DR.
Audrec SeTourne was a duelist from Lantan who was in Mulmaster.
Atia Scorvo () was a medusa member of the Cult of the Black Earth in the Earthspur Mountains in 1491 DR.

Audara Imryth was a cleric of Mystra and a potion-seller in Westgate in 1370 DR. Secretly, she was a member of the Harpers, watching over the city. Audara was affiliated with the Harper branch based in Shadowdale and had a strained relationship with fellow local Harper Jamal, whom she did not trust. In case of necessity, she would agree to work with her, however.
Askalan Larcloaks was a gnome wheelwright in Immerford in Cormyr.
Austrus Flambrant was a noble in Cormyr and the lord of Flambrant House.

Astilabor () was the neutral dragon goddess of acquisitiveness and wealth. She represented the draconic desire to acquire and treasure wealth and by doing so gain status, and so she was, in a way, the archetype of dragonkind.
Augrek Brighthelm was a deputy in Bryn Shander sometime after the War of the Silver Marches.
Aunglass Roaryl was a legendary hero of Eskorn, Laerakond, and the founder of the Roaryl dynasty.

Ausuriel, also known as the Blind Goat or simply Clyde, was a deva that acted as the patron angel of lost children. She held the role of Herald of Shiallia, the goddess of fertility and exarch of Mielikki. She came down to Faerûn numerous times throughout the late 15 century DR, appearing in the lands of the Moonsea and the nation of Elturgard.
Atsuo Toru was a farmer in Kudoku and secretly one of the Five Deadly Shadows in 1479 DR.
Aubaerus () was a hierophant druid in the Thunder Peaks area in 1357 DR.
Aslyn Belark was a member of the Belark merchant family in Delzimmer circa the Year of Rogue Dragons, 1373 DR.
Askulder, known as the "Hand of Tiamat", was the High Suikh (king) of the city-state of Ormpur on the edge of Lapaliiya in southwest Faerûn at the beginning of the 14 century DR.
Atrion was a member of the Freedom Riders under the command of Randal Morn in Shadowdale in the mid–14 century DR.
Athror Baergil (1301 – 1391 DR) was a wealthy and successful mill owner who resided in northern Sembia.
Astele Keene, better known as Nine-Fingers, was the leader of the Guild, the criminal organization that operated within Baldur's Gate during the 15 century DR.

Asojano was a chimera that dwelled within the realm of Avernus within the Nine Hells in the late 15 century DR. Asojano made its home within a colossal dragon skull near the Monument to Tiamat. Asojano was an ally of the dragonborn Arkhan the Cruel around 1494 DR. Like Arkhan, Asojano lived its life in services to the deity Tiamat.

Aubleth Crownsilver was a member of the noble House Crownsilver in Cormyr around the turn of the 11 century DR. He was a courtier and a member of the Griffon Guard—an elite unit of knights that rode griffons.
Aun Argent was a devout follower of Lathander that served within the Order of the Aster during the mid–14 century DR.
Auleethaea Cormaeril was a member of House Cormaeril and served as a lady-in-waiting to Queen Alvandira of Cormyr in the late 12 and early 13 centuries DR.
Atremus Bellwether was a caravaneer of northwest Faerûn in the mid–14 century DR.
Asohs the Daring was a halfling that worked as an administrator at Holyhands House in the North Ward of Waterdeep in the . He and his two brothers were known as the Defenders Three.

Athan was an exprerienced human adventurer, who was entrusted by Elminster with the Gauntlets of Moander, a legendary artifact, in order to lead a group of heroes into the ruins of Myth Drannor in leu of the mysterious resurgence of the pool of radiance in Phlan in 1369 DR.
Atenas Swift was the proprietor of Frozenfar Expeditions during the late 15 century DR.
Aunsible Durn was a smith in the town of Ghars in Cormyr in the mid–14 century DR. His smithy had no name, for there was no other in town.
Avaline Vraemaril was an elven attendant at Mystra's Arms in the late mid-to-late 15 century DR.
Aurora Brightday was a human proxy of the Faerûnian power known as Lathander.
Aswal al-Mutiq was Caliph of In'aash when the Law of the Loregiver spread throughout Zakhara, the Land of Fate.

Athis Al-Din was the fiance of Sithal Al-Husn. After Habrauk Al-Nirin kidnapped the princess, he led his troops in numerous attacks against the Al-Alisk clan; he continued to lead the charge after his death.
High and Most Beautiful Priestess Aumraeya Ulmdrin was the high priestess of the Firehair's House, a temple dedicated to Sune, in Selgaunt, Sembia, in the mid–14 century DR.
Askarran was a warrior and sage inhabiting Selgaunt in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Atlavast was a Loremaster of Oghma and a self-appointed keeper of the library at the House of Knowledge in Neverwinter in the late 15 century DR.
Auglaer was an inhabitant of Wright's Ferry in Featherdale in the .

High Priestess Aummerglau Tistrin, who was also called the Sun of Ordulin because of her legendary beauty, was the ranking priest of the House of Revels, a temple dedicated to Sune, in Ordulin in the .
Augustavus Cale was the leader, founder, and the guild master of the Trade of Blades guild and freehouse of Neverwinter.
Auldo Morim lived in the village of Eveningstar during the late 14 century DR.
Blademajor Aubric Nihmedu was a well-respected citizen of Evereska that served as one of the Swords of Evereska as of the late 14 century DR.
Athelstan Meiados was a Tormtar paladin in the city-state of Saelmur, in the Land of the Lions region of south Faerûn, in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Athaeal, also known as the Witch-Queen of Evermeet, was the author of the Musings of a Witch-Queen in Exile‎ in the 3 century DR.
Auntie Unk was a sea hag in the Thunder Cliff Caves in the late 15 century DR. She and her sisters Nana Pocktuss and Granny Muyuk formed a sea hag coven.
Asrai, also referred to as water sprites in the Beastlands and Sjöra on Ysgard, were shy, delicate and elusive faeries that lived in deep waters.
Aswansea was a moon elf priest of Tyr inhabiting the city of Daggerford in the Western Heartlands during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Asiyra Boldwinter was an innkeep inhabiting the city of Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Aldenuth Orbrymm was a tavern owner inhabiting the city of Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Auldo Chaserperi was a member of the Chaserperi clan of mages of the late mid-14 century DR.
Atham One-Eye was a smith from Suzail, the capital of Cormyr, who was active in the early 14 century DR.

Adyat al Hayat was a horse trader in the town of Bralizzar. They were known to be active in the mid-14 century DR. Their shop was just past Qatrun Medrusa's store, down an alleyway on the west side of the bazaar.
Lady Aurae Shaeremae was an elf of House Shaeremae in Cormanthor in the 3 century DR.
Lord Auglamyr was an inhabitant of Cormanthyr in the 3 century DR, and the head of House Auglamyr.
Lord Aulauthar Orbryn was a mage of Cormanthyr working in the 3 century DR.
Athtar Nlossae was an inhabitant of Cormanthor in the 3 century DR.

Aubree Lucent was a paladin of Torm and member of the Hellriders who served Elturel with honor during the late 15 century DR. She was among those within the city immediately following its Descent to the Nine Hells, and famously confronted a powerful archdevil during her adventures.
Aszerra Untlimmer was a priestess of Shaundakul, the Rider of the Winds, during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Avalor was the Treespeaker of the elves of the Wealdath, the great forest found in the realm of Tethyr.
Askalath was a mage who once resided on the isle of Askalet in the Sea of Swords, many centuries before the 14 century DR.
Lady Asmrae Barelder was the wife of Lord Montror Barelder, head of the Barelder family in the 15 century DR.
Aszloakh the Hooded was the finhead saurial who was in charge of The Fool's Altar dedicated to Finder Wyvernspur, located in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Ason was pickpocket brother of Ginia the courtesan from the isle of Brynnlaw in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Aumlar Chaunthoun was a Zhentarim mage of the mid-14 century DR.

Dawnmaster Askell Stockhold was one of four devoted leaders of the Rosymorn Monastery in the Western Heartlands, who died before the late 15 century DR and the monastery's fall to the githyanki invaders.
Asparagus Mhallie was a dairy goat farmer, displaced by The Absolute, and as a refugee, sought shelter in Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.
Aspar was a Netherese priest who worked as a moneychanger in Karsus Enclave until its destruction in . She took fees of about 6–15% on each transaction.
Augur Harxkellan was an orator from the Lower City of Baldur's Gate in late 15 century DR.
Lord-prince Asmuth was a nobleman from Zhentil Keep in the mid–13 century DR. His younger brother Manshoon eliminated him to secure his position.
Astrala, sometimes spelled Astralla, was a human waitress who served tables at the Golden Goblet Inn in Mossbridges in the late 14 century DR.
Aumanas Kordran was a War Wizard of Cormyr in the late 15 century DR.
Athlar was a highknight of Cormyr in the late 15 century DR.
Atrocious was a flesh hound – a chimera like monstrosity of animated beast part, created by Luvia Bloodmire in the late 14 century DR.
Assassin imps were a specialized variety of imp from the Nine Hells. As per the name, they were among the deadliest of the imp varieties, being specially practiced in the murder of the helpless.
Asta Jegg'Dralnoc was a powerful Chosen of Lolth of House Jegg'Dralnoc, who wandered the Demonweb Pits during the 15 century DR.

Field Marshal Augustin Bambulozzi was a mercenary general from the Whamite Isles. Augustin's allegiances could be bought in a series of wild conflicts between various nations and pirates of the Whamite Isles at some point prior to the mass death of the population in the .
Atson was a potions merchant from Luskan during the late 15 century DR.
Avarilous was a mercenary spy who posed as a merchant and was active across Faerûn.
Asta the Deep-Minded was an elder dwarf woman who followed Hal Stoutheart's Tethyamar expedition in the 1480s DR.
Auvrarn Labraster was a merchant from Waterdeep in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. He was part of an obscure, nameless intrigue that was uncovered by the Seven Sisters.
Ate`Niah was the Serene Matriarch of Synnoria on the Moonshae Isles and ruler of the Llewyrr elves through the 14 and 15 centuries DR.
Asmartha was the innkeeper at Myrkiel's Rest in Narthil during the mid-3 century DR.
Master Scout Atrezt Dun'Robar was a drow soldier that served House Dun'Robar during the 1480s DR.
Aunsiber was a steward of Narthil in the Western Heartlands in the 3 century DR.

Lord Askepel was a leader of the Knights of Synnoria on the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles during the late 15 century DR. He was a key participant in a Synnorian plot to overthrow the ruling leShay of Sarifal.
Astral searchers were mindless creatures of nebulous humanoid shape whose only driving action was to invade the material plane and possess a body, thereby becoming sentient.
Brother Aurelius was a scholarly servant of the Silver Flame in the world of Eberron.
Ate Onah was the Serene Matriarch of Chrysalis on the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles as of the turn of the 16 century DR, and was thus ruler of the Llewyrr elves.
Athanial the Wind was an explorer and writer from Procampur in the Vast in the mid-to-late 14 century DR, and even be a member of the Guild of Shadows and a shadow walker.
Augrathar Buruin, known as the "High Huntmaster of Vaunted Malar", was a high priest of Malar in Cormyr.
Athalon Darvae was a textiles merchant from Saerloon who resided in Cormyr. He once thought of moving to Suzail but changed his mind.

Baatezu (; ) were the dominant race of devils in the Nine Hells, once evil mortals whose souls, due to diabolical deed or infernal contract, were condemned to Baator. Stripped of individuality through vile torture and remade from the divine energy harvested from the collective corrupted, the baatezu institutionalized suffering, ascending to tyranny on the backs of the damned.

King Azoun Obarskyr IV ( ) of Cormyr was the king of Cormyr from 1336 DR to 1371 DR and a member of the Purple Dragon Knights. During his reign, the kingdom experienced unprecedented economic growth. He was killed in the Goblin War by Nalavarauthatoryl. He was counted as a mythic sovereign.
Azers ( ; ) were elemental creatures native to the Elemental Plane of Fire and Elemental Chaos.

Baervan Wildwanderer () was the gnome god (particularly identified with forest gnomes) of forests, travel, and nature. The Forest Gnome was the closest thing the gnomes had to a druidic deity, for the Masked Leaf was always attentive to the concerns of the wild while still keeping a close eye on his gnome charges.

Baerelus the Bold was a satyr and local expert on the lore, flora, and fauna of the King's Forest of Cormyr around 1367 DR. Beloved by the people, he enjoyed serving as a guide and source of wise advice to many young Cormyreans within the area. He was kept informed of what was going on within Cormyr by the confessions of the young folk he spoke to in his daily travels. King Azoun IV was known to stop by the forest with a sumptuous meal to learn from Baerelus' experience. While he wouldn't reveal any secrets told to him in confidence, Baerelus gave the king a shrewd picture of the nation of Cormyr. Azoun was keen on heeding most of what Baerelus told him.

Baerauble Etharr (later Baerauble the Venerable and Baerauble the Wise) was a Netherese wizard who lived for many years in the company of the elves inhabiting Cormanthyr, and later became the first Royal Magician of Cormyr.

Azoun I (; full name Azoun Obarskyr) was the 51 king of Cormyr, reigning from 391–425 DR. He was the son of King Anglond of the Obarskyr dynasty, and was titled "the Crown Prince of Battles" for his campaigns as a prince.
Azoun Rhigaerd Palaghard Duar Obarskyr V () was the 71 king of Cormyr, having inherited the throne after the death of his grandfather, Azoun IV,
Ayala Windspear was an elf Harper of the late 14 century DR who saved Drogan Droganson's life after the kobold attack on Hilltop.
Baeron Silmaeril was one of the original Lords of Waterdeep. Along with Shilarn, he overthrew the Lords Magister Ehlemm Zoar and Lhorar Gildeggh to restore the government of Waterdeep.

Bahgtru () was the orc god of pure, physical strength and patron of the average orc, a deity as awesomely strong as he was utterly oafish. He embodied the merciless might with which orcs overwhelmed their enemies, driving each weapon to do as much damage as possible. Son of Gruumsh and the Cave Mother Luthic, the Leg-Breaker was the orc symbol of tribalistic loyalty and unstoppable power, a champion of brutal, senseless violence.
Avery Schell was a cleric of Deneir and one of the headmasters of the Edificant Library in the mid–14 century DR. He was the substitute father of Cadderly Bonaduce.

Bala was a goddess of music in Zakhara and emphasized the importance of music to lift the spirit and mitigate suffering. She was a local goddess who was worshiped in the city of Mahabba, but her faith was outlawed and driven underground by the Pantheists. In this persecution her followers spread to other cities. Their sometimes violent resistance against their oppressors brought the goddess the epithet "of Ill Tidings". Bala's symbol was a zither. The goddess has been described as a colorfully but modestly dressed, middle-aged woman who played her zither in a way that enchanted gods and genies. Holy slayers of the Final Chord followed Bala's teachings.

Baalzebul,() formerly an archon known as Triel, was the lord of Maladomini and most infamous archdevil next to Asmodeus himself. He was known as the Lord of the Flies because his webs of intrigue were so tightly woven that not even flies could escape, but the form he was cursed with by Asmodeus earned him a new, hated title; The Slug Archduke. Eventually he managed to overcome this wretched state and return to his previous glory, and if only to retain it, had never told a lie to his kin since.

Azhir Kren was the tharchioness of Gauros in Thay, during the 14 century DR. She constantly plotted and schemed to invade the realm of Rashemen to the north, in the years following her mother's death.
Azariah Craulnober (pronounced ah-ZAH-ree-ah) was the daughter of Elaith Craulnober, a moon elf crime lord of Waterdeep.

Baernaloths, also known as the Baern, were legendary fiends of the Gray Wastes, as devoid of emotion and color as the plane itself and among the multiverse's biggest enigmas. Thought to be a type of yugoloth, rumors claimed they spawned not just the daemons, but also the demons, demodands, and devils, and they allegedly knew the most about all creatures of the Lower Planes.
Azmaer Dhuurniv was the last drow marshal of the Twisted Tower of Ashaba in Shadowdale in the early 10 century DR.
Azalar Falconhand was a ranger of Mielikki and the son of Dove and Florin Falconhand.
Azul, also known as Calor, was the Maztican god of rain and water.
Bacars were intelligent, ant-like creatures living in the valley of Ixtzul in Maztica.
Baerill was a human woman living in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr. She was one of the proprietors of the Wyvern Watch Inn.
Axithar was a balor lord whose armies invaded the House of the Triad after the fall of Mystra.
Badrazel was a male balor and the chief lieutenant of Kurgoth Hellspawn during the Silence of Lolth.
Azbara Jos was a Red Wizard of Thay and a member of the faction loyal to Rath Modar.
Bael An Ashok was the proprietor of the Grand Emporium in Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR.
Azanza Mizzrym was the leader of the House Mizzrym contingent that controlled the ruins of Sulasspryn in 1367 DR.
Bahramiyah al-Musafir was a caravan master from Hiyal in Zakhara in 1367 DR.
Avimmuck Wanderfoot was the Cloakmaster of the Caravan Sect of the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR.
Baerick Hammerstone was a dwarf master of the black ice in Icewind Dale in 1485 DR.
Avner of Hartsvale was a thief and scout in Hartsvale in the 14 century DR.
Aya Glenmiir was an elven wizard in Phlan during the Tyranny of Dragons.

Baerildo Obarskyr was the 34th Obarskyr monarch and a king of Cormyr in name, but he was murdered while still an infant by his wicked grandaunt. He was succeeded by his father's half-brother Belmuth "the Bastard".
Baerovus I was a king of Cormyr. He succeeded his father Proster Obarskyr as only heir and was followed by his second son, Palaghard I.
Azak Throm () was a Red Wizard of Thay diplomat in Mulmaster in 1491 DR.
Aziz al-Asra was a mercenary who lived within the fortress of Sarahin in 1367 DR.
Bahija Jalin was a potion vendor who lived in Huzuz in 1367 DR.
Baar Tworgeir was a carpenter living in Hillsfar in the late 15 century DR.
Aziz Jomini was an elven associate of the Mosque of Free Haku in 1367 DR.
Badiat al-Farif was a member of the court of Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
Bagatur Jokai was a commander within the Grand Army of the Tuigan during the mid 14 century DR.
Baga Choki was a Tuigan warrior and member of the Grand Army of the Tuigan during the mid 14 century DR.
Aziz min Hajama was a dwarven moralist who served as the commander of the Gate of Revelations within the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
Bahija al-Kesir was a human pragmatist within the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
Bacao Foo was a merchant in Suijeng in Shou Lung in 1358 DR.
Awang Sophir was a monk from Petan who participated at the Komite in Shou Lung in 1358 DR.
Azhakar was a talking bird who lived in Zakhara, the Land of Fate, in 1367 DR.
Ayesha al-Rumi was a holy slayer inhabiting Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.
Baiyosho Degi was a monk member of the Tairo in Wa around 1357 DR.
Ayana No-Shui was a wu jen in the Northern Wastes of Kara-Tur around 1357 DR.
Baergon Bluesword was a cleric of Tempus in Daggerford around 1370 DR.
Badiat bint Malin was an influential sha'ir who lived in Kadarasto in 1367 DR.
Baerdeth Malagar was the High Priest or Huntmaster of the High House of the Hunt, a temple devoted to the worship of Malar in Zhentil Keep in 1358 DR.
Baergus was a merchant from Zhentil Keep who focused on the trade of hardware.
Baern Harbrow was a War Wizard of Cormyr in Suzail during the late 15 century DR.
Baert Ghalhunt was one of Marlin Stormserpent's henchmen in the late 15 century DR.
Avnon Des was First Demarch of Mask in the Hall of Shadows in Elgrin Fau, a city from another world that was moved to the Plane of Shadow.
Baishiria was a dragonborn of Abeir, and one of the ancestors of Clan Kepeshkmolik.
Avos the Fisher was the leader of the Quippers, a street gang in the Scab, a notorious slum of Selgaunt, in the late 14 century DR.
